title: LOKAYAN 2026 – INDIAN NAVAL SHIP SUDARSHINI DEPARTS LISBON AFTER THREE-DAY PORT CALL
body_text:
The Indian Navy’s sail training ship INS Sudarshini concluded her three-day port call at Lisbon, Portugal, on 25 Aug 2026 , as part of her ongoing Lokayan 26 transoceanic expedition.
During the port call, the Commanding Officer of INS Sudarshini called on Rear Admiral Miguel Bessa Pacheco, Commandant, Portuguese Naval Academy, and Rear Admiral Joao Paulo Silva Pereira, Deputy Fleet Commander, Portuguese Navy . The engagements reinforced the institutional ties and mutual understanding between the two navies. As part of the professional engagements, sea trainees from the Indian Navy visited the Portuguese Naval Academy (Escola Naval), where they interacted with their Portuguese counterparts, toured the historic campus and training facilities, and exchanged perspectives on seamanship and tall-ship sail training. The port call also featured a deck reception onboard with senior Portuguese military officials, members of the diplomatic corps and the Indian diaspora.
The visit of INS Sudarshini to Portuguese ports of Ponta Delgada and Lisbon underscores the enduring maritime cooperation and partnership between the two nations.
***
VM/AS

enrichment.summary: INS Sudarshini, the Indian Navy's sail training ship, completed a three-day port call at Lisbon, Portugal, concluding on 25 August 2026 as part of its Lokayan 26 transoceanic expedition. During the visit, the ship's Commanding Officer met senior Portuguese Navy officials, sea trainees visited the Portuguese Naval Academy, and a deck reception was held with diplomats and the Indian diaspora. The visit followed an earlier stop at Ponta Delgada and highlights ongoing maritime cooperation between India and Portugal.
enrichment.context:
INS Sudarshini is a sail training ship of the Indian Navy used to train young officers in traditional seamanship and to conduct goodwill and diplomatic outreach voyages abroad, often called 'sail diplomacy'. Such expeditions, including the recurring 'Lokayan' series, are part of India's broader naval diplomacy efforts to strengthen bilateral defence ties, enhance the Navy's global visibility, and project soft power through cultural and training exchanges rather than combat operations. These port calls typically involve interactions between naval academies, officer exchanges, and outreach to the Indian diaspora, reflecting India's expanding maritime engagement beyond its immediate neighbourhood into Europe and the Atlantic.

This event is largely a routine goodwill visit with no new policy announcement, agreement, or strategic shift, and thus holds limited standalone examination value beyond general awareness of India's naval training ships and defence diplomacy initiatives.
